newsitem.title: USA: U.S stocks seen to dip at open after 7 day streak.
newsitem.headline: U.S stocks seen to dip at open after 7 day streak.

text.p: Wall Street stocks open slightly lower Friday, awaiting some key economic data, after last night's fireworks when stocks a record closing high.
It was the first time ever the Dow topped the 6300 mark, and its seventh consecutive new closing high, matching a record set in February 5 to 13 earlier this year.
"We've got some economic news coming, and with the expiration of options, we'll probably see stocks open a bit on the weak side," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
Hildegard Zagorski, Prudential Securities analyst, said, "It looks like a lower opening, but we seem to open lower and mixed every morning lately."
At 1415 GMT, the government will release October industrial production, which economists expect to be flat, and capacity use, forecast to drop to 83.0 percent from 83.3 percent in the prior month.
